about: Model-provider confinement falsifiers (cc-model-confine lane, tasks 006, 004, 011, 013, 010, 012, 014, 015, 016 and 017). Every entry but F-cc1e, F-cc8-rm-journal, F-cc15a, F-cc15b, F-cc15c, F-cc16a, F-cc16b, F-cc16c, F-cc17a, F-cc17b, F-cc19a, F-cc19b, F-cc29a, F-cc30b, F-cc30c, F-cc30d, F-cc30e F-cc31a, F-cc40a and F-cc41a edits capsules/model-provider/confine.sb, which sandbox-exec reads at each launch, so a mutated profile needs no rebuild. Those twenty edit capsules/model-provider/tests/confine/main.rs, so the runner rebuilds the test for them; the runner's startup recovery restores that file after a killed run. F-cc1a turns (deny default) into (allow default) and F-cc1b widens the journal read/write grant from STORAGE_ROOT to STORAGE_PARENT; model_outside_write_denied then fails because the redirected journal write succeeds. F-cc1c widens the STORAGE_PARENT read from the parent alone to its subtree; model_outside_read_denied then fails because the run record outside STORAGE_ROOT is read and returned. F-cc1d leaves the STORAGE_ROOT grant write-only; model_outside_read_denied then fails at its first init, which cannot inspect the journal root. F-cc1e removes that test's one fixture rule from capsules/model-provider/tests/confine/main.rs, so the runner rebuilds the test; runs_get then stops at the record's existence check instead of its open, and the test fails. Each F-cc1-rm entry removes one allow rule and model_provider_ops_under_profile fails. F-cc7a turns (deny default) into (allow default) and F-cc7b keeps (deny default) and adds one (allow file-read*) after the last rule; model_local_offer_fails_closed_under_profile then fails because the init with a local engine offer answers ok. F-cc8a turns (deny default) into (allow default); model_outside_create_reports_access_denied then fails because the redirected init answers ok. F-cc8c keeps (deny default) and adds one (allow file-write* (subpath (param "STORAGE_PARENT"))) after the STORAGE_ROOT rule; the redirected journal create then succeeds, runs/ appears under the outside sibling, and the same test fails because init no longer answers journal_access_denied. F-cc8-rm-journal removes that test's one fixture rule, a metadata read of the redirected journal root, from capsules/model-provider/tests/confine/main.rs; the sandbox then refuses the inspect before the create, init answers journal_corrupt, and the test fails. F-cc10a turns (deny default) into (allow default) and removes (deny network*), because (allow default) alone leaves (deny network*) refusing the connect; F-cc10b keeps (deny default) and turns (deny network*) into (allow network*); model_hosted_run_fails_closed_under_profile then fails because the hosted run's request reaches the test's Runtime socket stand-in. Removing (deny network*) alone changes no behaviour, because (deny default) still refuses the connect, so only the one profile-shape check holds that removal. F-cc12a deletes (deny network*) and uses command wallet, because that check, both_file_profiles_bind_one_storage_parameter_contract, is in the wallet crate; the check then refuses the model profile with "model-provider must deny the network explicitly with (deny network*)". The check reads this profile from disk at each run and starts no sandbox, so F-cc12a needs no sandbox. F-cc14a turns (deny default) into (allow default); F-cc14b and F-cc14c keep the exec rule word for word and add one (allow process-exec) or one (allow process-exec (subpath (param "STORAGE_ROOT"))) after it, so both still pass the one shape check; model_unbound_program_refused_under_profile then fails because a byte-identical copy of the provider binary under STORAGE_ROOT starts and answers init while the real binary is bound as PROVIDER_EXECUTABLE. F-cc15a, F-cc15b and F-cc15c each undo one part of how the test's Runtime socket stand-in counts connections, the count model_hosted_run_fails_closed_under_profile reads as its evidence that no connection came. F-cc15a moves the count from the accept to after the request has been read, so runtime_socket_stand_in_counts_a_silent_connection fails: a connection that sends nothing is not counted. F-cc15b removes the final observation's accepts of the connections still queued, so runtime_socket_stand_in_drains_queued_connections counts neither of its two queued clients. F-cc15c serves each connection on the accept loop itself, so runtime_socket_stand_in_accepts_behind_a_silent_connection fails: a request behind a silent connection waits for that connection's read timeout. Those three tests start no provider and no sandbox. F-cc16a, F-cc16b and F-cc16c each undo one part of how the test's one wait loop holds its deadline, the FIXTURE_EVENT_TIMEOUT within which the hosted run must settle. F-cc16a returns a terminal reply before the deadline check, so hosted_run_wait_fails_a_reply_after_its_deadline fails: a terminal reply read after the deadline is accepted. F-cc16b gives each poll FIXTURE_EVENT_TIMEOUT instead of the time left, so the same test fails: its first poll is given more than the 50 ms left, so a poll may wait past the deadline. F-cc16c gives the request path's one receive FIXTURE_EVENT_TIMEOUT instead of the wait it is given, so hosted_run_wait_times_out_without_a_reply fails: a runs_get with no answer waits past the deadline. hosted_run_wait_fails_a_reply_after_its_deadline starts no provider and no sandbox. hosted_run_wait_times_out_without_a_reply starts /bin/sleep so that receive can time out; it starts no provider binary and no sandbox. F-cc17a returns Ok(false) from the declared-OS branch of sandbox_gate, so sandbox_gate_fails_instead_of_skipping_on_a_declared_os fails: the macos case with the missing path is no longer Err. F-cc17b returns false from the error arm of sandbox_available instead of failing the test, so sandbox_available_fails_for_macos_when_sandbox_exec_is_missing fails: a missing sandbox-exec on macos returns, and the confined test would pass by skipping. Those two tests start no process and need no sandbox. F-cc19a starts the program directly, without sandbox-exec, when the profile file does not exist, so startup_is_refused_when_the_profile_cannot_be_applied fails: case (a)'s launch starts the provider unconfined, it answers init, and the test fails at its first check. F-cc19b keeps none of the stderr lines Provider::ended reads, so the same test fails: case (a) still exits 65, but no line gives sandbox-exec's reason. The confined tests need /usr/bin/sandbox-exec and, when sandbox-exec is missing, skip only off macOS and fail on a Mac without it, so this list is a Mac gate. Files are relative to examples/agent-host. F-cc29a skips the digest compare in refuse_changed_provider_executable, so the changed file starts. F-cc30a appends one allow rule that no declared right and no platform baseline names. F-cc30b points the trace at a fixture that drops the bound-executable right. F-cc30c points it at a fixture whose storage right has no rule. F-cc30d points it at a fixture where two rights claim the exec rule. F-cc30e points it at a fixture rule that is not an allow line. F-cc30f repeats the STORAGE_ROOT allow. allow_rules_trace_to_declared_rights fails for each. F-cc31a renames model_provider_ops_under_profile, so operations_section_cites_existing_tests no longer finds that function. F-cc35b appends (allow sysctl-write) beside the startup-sysctl pin, so platform_baseline_rules_stay_narrow fails. F-cc35c, F-cc35d and F-cc35e keep both startup pins and add literal reads whose filenames contain STORAGE_ROOT, STORAGE_PARENT or PROVIDER_EXECUTABLE; platform_baseline_rules_stay_narrow rejects each wider path. F-cc35f keeps both startup pins and appends (allow file-write* (literal "/tmp/cc35-write-only")) to the profile, so platform_baseline_rules_stay_narrow fails. F-cc35g keeps both startup pins and appends (allow file* (literal "/tmp/cc35-wildcard")) to the profile, so platform_baseline_rules_stay_narrow fails. F-cc35a widens startup-root-directory from file-read-data to file-read*, so platform_baseline_rules_stay_narrow fails. F-cc36a removes the last parenthesis of the STORAGE_ROOT allow, so byte_different_file_at_bound_path_starts exits 65 and fails because the profile did not apply. F-cc37a writes an allow after (deny network*) on that same line, so allow_rules_trace_to_declared_rights fails because that allow has no declared right and no platform baseline. F-cc38a writes (allow on its own line after the root pin, then file-read* (literal "/tmp/cc-unclosed")) on the next line, so platform_baseline_rules_stay_narrow fails because the allow form does not close. F-cc39a writes a line ( after the root pin, then allow file-read* (literal "/tmp/cc-split-allow")) on the next line, so platform_baseline_rules_stay_narrow and allow_rules_trace_to_declared_rights fail because the allow form does not close. F-cc40a makes falsifier_section_ids_match return Ok before it compares, so falsifier_section_names_every_list_id fails because a table that drops F-cc39a is accepted. F-cc41a makes standin_profile return the oracle file and ignore the declared value, so generated_model_profile_matches_the_oracle fails because a changed declared rule still matches the oracle.
